items.title: Fact-Checking Using AI
items.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) can both correct inaccurate beliefs (1, 2, 3) and manipulate attitudes (4, 5, 6). As LLMs are increasingly deployed as fact-checkers on social media, their impact depends not only on the models’ technical capability, but also on the choices of their designers and the attitudes and behaviors of platform users. Here, we shed light on all three dimensions of this sociotechnical system. We analyze an exhaustive sample of 1,555,281 English-language fact-check requests sent to Grok and Perplexity bots on X from February through September 2025 and a random sample of 184,124 fact-checks from Grok from September 2025 to August 2026. We also benchmark 19 frontier LLMs against professional fact-checkers’ evaluations of hundreds of news headlines, and conduct a preregistered survey experiment (N=1,592) to evaluate correction efficacy. On the user side, Grok requesters skew heavily Republican; familiarity with and trust in specific LLMs vary substantially, such that trust in AI is no longer a unitary construct; and revealing that a fact-check comes from Grok reduces belief updating among Democrats while increasing belief updating among Republicans. Examining LLM outputs, we find that from a technical perspective, LLM fact-checks can match or exceed agreement among professional fact-checkers. Yet we also show that this capacity is readily undermined by designers’ choices: for example, restricting sources (e.g. Truth Social AI) or disabling search can degrade accuracy. Designers and users, more so than technical capability, are now the primary binding constraints.

items.title: Factors Associated With Surgical Faculty’s Desire to Leave or Stay at Their Jobs
items.abstract: Importance: Surgical faculty turnover in academic centers causes interruptions in continuity of patient care, trainee education, and loss of funding from research and clinical revenue, while burdening departments with new recruitment efforts. Objective: To identify variables associated with surgical faculty's desire both to leave and to stay in their job. Design, Setting, and Participants: A cross-sectional 67-item survey based on the job demands-resources model was administered to 452 surgical faculty at 10 medical centers across the US from February 2025 to September 2025. Demographics and factors related to attrition/intent to leave/retention were queried. Satisfaction was measured on a 5-point Likert scale. Reliability was high (Cronbach α > 0.70). χ2 testing and Mann-Whitney U tests were used for analysis. These data were analyzed from September 2025 through February 2026. Exposures: Surgical faculty in full-time practice at 1 of 10 medical centers. Main Outcomes and Measures: The primary outcome measure was surgical faculty seriously considering leaving (SCL) their current job. Secondary outcome was attrition from prior faculty position. Results: There were 209 respondents (response rate, 46.2% [209 of 452]); 59.4% were in their first job (FJ) after training, with 36.7% serving as assistant professors, 29.4% as associate professors, and 29.4% as full professors. Overall, 41.1% (95% CI, 34.3%-48.1%) reported SCL. SCL was higher for FJ (47.2%; 95% CI, 38.1%-56.4% vs 32.1%; 95% CI, 22.4%-43.2% for non-FJ faculty [P = .03]), those working longer clinical hours (50; 95% CI, 40-58.75 vs 40; 95% CI, 40-50; P = .05), and the university-academic SCL rate (45.5% [55 of 121]) vs university-affiliated SCL (48% [24 of 50]) vs nonprofit independent SCL (16.7% [6 of 36]) (P = .004). The top reasons cited for SCL were unhappiness with current leadership/governance (60% strongly agreed/agreed), lacking work-life balance (51.8%), feeling burnout (51.8%), and seeking new leadership opportunities (48.2%). Age, gender, race and ethnicity, geographic region, and academic rank were not associated with SCL. The most cited reasons for why faculty stayed in their present position were enjoying teaching trainees, relationship with colleagues, and the variety of cases. Conclusions and Relevance: These results demonstrated that a significant number of surgical faculty reported seriously considering leaving their positions. The results provide actionable insights for improving retention, including greater engagement from departmental leadership and the creation of a nurturing, collaborative environment with career advancement opportunities.

items.title: Feasibility and Usability of Head-Mounted Display Augmented Reality During Routine Radiological Interventions: The Prospective AZURION-AR Study
items.abstract: PURPOSE: To evaluate the feasibility, usability, and perceived workload of the AZURION-AR augmented reality (AR) medical device during routine interventional radiology procedures in a real-world clinical setting. MATERIALS AND METHODS: This prospective, single-center, single-arm feasibility study included six interventional radiologists performing 34 AR-assisted vascular and non-vascular procedures. The AZURION-AR system projected virtual monitor and touchscreen interfaces within the operator's visual field. Post-procedural structured interviews and standardized 5-point Likert questionnaires assessed usability (System Usability Scale, SUS; 1-5 per item, max score: 100), workload (NASA Task Load Index, NASA-TLX; 0-21 per domain), and image quality (1-5 scale). RESULTS: Continuous head-mounted display use throughout the procedure occurred in 20 cases (58%); mean wearing time was 40 min [5-140 min] versus a mean procedure duration of 59 min [20-240 min]. Mean SUS score was 64.5 ± 11.1, indicating moderate usability with considerable inter-operator variability. Mean NASA-TLX score was 7.6 ± 1.4, reflecting acceptable workload. Mean image quality score was 3.5 ± 0.6, with substantial variability across interventions. Scores tended to be lower in vascular and complex drainage procedures, reflecting increased effort and frustration, reduced anatomical detail, limited spatial resolution, and technical issues such as battery depletion and signal lag. CONCLUSION: The AZURION-AR medical device proved feasible for use during routine interventional radiology offering unanimously rated perceived ergonomic advantages. Although usability was moderate, limitations in image resolution, technical reliability, and battery life require further refinement before reliable routine clinical implementation can be achieved, particularly for procedures requiring high spatial resolution and detailed anatomical assessment.

items.title: Federating Governance: How Community Rules Scale with Mastodon Servers
items.abstract: The rise of decentralized social media platforms like Mastodon and Bluesky highlights the challenge of scaling self-governance and moderation. As communities grow, they face new issues that demand increasingly complex governance structures. However, as moderation is mainly volunteer-driven, there is limited formal guidance on how community rules and moderation practices should evolve with growth. This study investigates how moderation scale with Mastodon instances by analyzing community rules across servers of varying sizes. We categorize these rules to identify key governance priorities and find that these priorities are remarkably consistent across instance sizes: rules addressing problematic content, such as harassment, hate speech, and illegal content, dominate regardless of scale. While smaller communities focus on narrower sets of topics, larger servers maintain a more balanced coverage of a broad range of topics. Our analysis of rule formalization reveals that community size strongly predicts rule development. As instances grow, their rules become more extensive and topically diverse, but also exhibit lower readability and linguistic diversity. In contrast, external federation interactions have a limited role, mainly associated with a broader scope of rules without substantially affecting their diversity or form. These findings highlight the relative influence of internal versus external factors, suggesting that local scaling pressures outweigh network-level dynamics in decentralized social media governance. The scaling pattern observed on Mastodon resemble those previously identified on centralized platforms such as Reddit, suggesting that community size imposes fundamental constraints on self-governance that transcend platform architectures.

items.title: FFM-CP: Cross-Backbone Fusion of Vision-Language Foundation Models for Few-Shot Computational Pathology
items.abstract: Pathology vision-language foundation models vary in performance across diseases and tasks, with no single model consistently performing best. The high cost of expert pathology annotation can also limit the labeled data available for task-specific adaptation. Combining complementary pretrained representations is a potential approach to these limitations, yet learning an effective fusion from few labeled examples remains challenging. We introduce Few-shot Fusion Foundation Models of Computational Pathology (FFM-CP), which is a framework that combines multiple pathology vision-language models in the few-shot learning setting. The framework first aligns heterogeneous representations using a closed-form Orthogonal Procrustes transformation estimated from corresponding support images. This alignment preserves within-model feature geometry without training an additional alignment network. Within the aligned space, a unified graph enables information exchange across backbones by jointly refining support-image features and visual and textual class prototypes. These refined representations support complementary text-prototype and case-retrieval branches that capture semantic class knowledge and within-class visual variation, respectively. Each branch learns to combine predictions from all ordered backbone pairs, allowing queries encoded by one model to draw on evidence represented by another. We evaluate three backbone combinations on six histopathology datasets at 4, 8, and 16 shots per class. FFM-CP achieves higher mean macro-F1 than the strongest individually adapted member of each fused set in 50 of 54 comparisons. These findings suggest that combining complementary pretrained representations can improve histopathological classification when annotations are limited.

items.title: Field grand challenge: beyond putting patients asleep: redefining the mission of anesthesiology
items.abstract: Modern surgery would not exist without the rise of anesthesiology. The introduction of anesthesiology as a clinical specialty during the 1930s and 1940s transformed medicine by removing pain and consciousness as the principal barriers to surgery. Subsequently, anesthesiology evolved beyond the administration of hypnotic and analgesic drugs; it became the medical specialty dedicated to preserving metabolic and hemodynamic homeostasis during one of the most profound stresses the human body can experience. Advances in pharmacology and technology accelerated this transformation, progressively increasing both precision and quality.Improved patient safety marked the second transformation of anesthesiology. Anesthesiologists recognized that excellence depended not only on individual expertise, i.e. the practice of anesthesia "as an art", but also on evidence-based knowledge, effective teamwork, communication, and learning from errors. Standardized monitoring, airway and crisis management algorithms, simulation-based education, human factors engineering, checklists, international safety standards, and continuous quality improvement initiatives have collectively reduced anesthesia-related mortality to historically low levels in many healthcare systems.Today, artificial intelligence, predictive analytics, closed-loop systems, and sophisticated monitoring technologies promise further improvements in intraoperative decision-making [1]. While safety remains an ongoing commitment, the traditional mission of anesthesiology-bringing patients safely through surgery-is approaching a level of maturity unimaginable only a few decades ago [2].Ironically, this extraordinary success now challenges anesthesiologists to redefine their raison d'être. For most patients exposed to surgery and anesthesia today, survival is an expected outcome.While this objective remains essential, it is not the only meaningful endpoint. A technically flawless anesthetic may still be followed by postoperative disability. Importantly, patients undergo surgical procedures to live longer, preserve their independence, remain cognitively intact, return to their families, resume work, or simply regain the ability to perform the activities that give meaning to their lives. These expectations represent a profound shift in perspective. The greatest challenge facing anesthesiology today is no longer how to safely guide a patient through surgery. It is how to influence what happens afterwards.Millions of patients each year continue to experience postoperative complications, prolonged disability, persistent pain, cognitive decline, psychological distress, delayed return to work, and loss of independence [3,4]. At the same time, the surgical population has been changing dramatically. Patients are older, frailer, and afflicted by multiple chronic diseases. Furthermore, surgical procedures are becoming increasingly ambitious and complex, while healthcare systems face unprecedented pressure to deliver high-quality care with limited resources. The future of anesthesiology therefore requires a transition from a process-oriented technical specialty to comprehensive outcome-oriented medicine [5].Improving recovery starts weeks before surgery through optimization of relevant co-morbid conditions, nutrition, and frailty by shared, multidisciplinary decision-making. Anesthetic care continues during surgery by individualized physiological management and evidence-based perioperative measures. It extends beyond discharge through pain management, rehabilitation, functional assessment, complication surveillance, and coordination with primary care and rehabilitation teams. In other words, anesthesiology has evolved from facilitating an operation to managing a trajectory. This broader vision also affects the way we assess patients. Frailty scores, nutritional screening, functional tests, biomarkers, cognitive evaluations, or postoperative patient-reported outcomes only become valuable when they trigger meaningful interventions.The growing complexity of perioperative care also calls for greater collaboration. Surgeons, intensivists, nurses, physiotherapists, nutrition specialists, psychologists, geriatricians, primary care physicians, engineers, and data scientists all contribute complementary expertise, and places anesthesiologists in a unique leadership role. Their expertise in physiology, pharmacology, pain management, critical care, and risk assessment naturally positions them to coordinate multidisciplinary perioperative pathways and ensure continuity across the patient's surgical journey. Emerging technologies will undoubtedly accelerate this transformation. Artificial intelligence may support risk prediction and real-time decision-making. Wearable devices and digital platforms will enable continuous monitoring beyond hospital walls. Predictive analytics may identify patients who would benefit most from prehabilitation, nutritional interventions, or enhanced postoperative surveillance.The future of the specialty will not be determined by incremental improvements in techniques and technologies alone, but by our ability to comprehend, predict, and modify the patient's entire perioperative trajectory. This requires a better understanding of recovery itself. Despite decades of advances in perioperative medicine, the biological mechanisms that determine why some patients rapidly regain function while others not, remain incompletely understood. Recovery is a complex and dynamic physiological process involving inflammation, metabolic alterations, resilience, psychological Achieving these goals will require moving towards a better understanding of when, in whom, and to what extent perioperative interventions affect outcomes that matter to patients. This includes, but is not limited to, refining the evidence surrounding the relationship between depth of anesthesia and electroencephalographic monitoring and postoperative cognitive outcomes, individualized hemodynamic management and cardiac or neurological outcomes, perioperative glycemic control and infectious complications, and perioperative nutritional interventions to enhance functional recovery and metabolic resilience.The future of anesthesiology therefore requires systematic integration of patient-reported outcomes, patient experience, disability-free survival, and long-term functional recovery into both clinical research and routine practice. Importantly, these outcomes should not merely be collected; they should inform clinical decision-making and help define individualized care plans [6]. Finally, the greatest challenge may not be discovering new interventions, but ensuring that existing evidence consistently reaches patients. Enhanced Recovery After Surgery (ERAS) pathways have demonstrated that coordinated, evidence-based perioperative care can substantially improve recovery, yet implementation remains highly variable across institutions and healthcare systems [7,8]. Closing this evidence-to-practice gap should become a research priority in its own right.As anesthesiology enters its third stage of development as an academic clinical specialty, Frontiers in Anesthesiology has the opportunity to become a catalyst for this transformation by fostering dialogue across traditional disciplinary boundaries and by promoting research that addresses questions that will shape perioperative care over the coming decades. The journal will serve as a multidisciplinary forum where ideas from all disciplines involved in perioperative care converge. Hence, the journal is committed to embrace the full spectrum of perioperative research. Basic and translational science remain essential to understand the mechanisms underlying recovery, while clinical trials, implementation studies, quality improvement initiatives, digital health innovations, and health systems research are indispensable to translate these discoveries into better care. Furthermore, we welcome research addressing contemporary challenges in precision perioperative medicine, artificial intelligence, and patients or relatives empowerment strategies to enhance recovery after surgery. Well-conducted negative studies also deserve visibility, as they refine our understanding of complex clinical research questions, prevent unnecessary interventions, and help redirect research efforts toward more promising strategies. In addition, educational contributions, illustrative clinical cases, and interdisciplinary perspectives that generate discussion or provide practical insights into perioperative care will also be considered.We hope that Frontiers in Anesthesiology will become the home for research that embraces this broader vision-research that not only explains perioperative physiology, but changes clinical practice, informs healthcare policy, and improves the outcomes that matter most to patients.

items.title: Forced Oscillations in Power Systems Induced by Data Centers Hosting AI Workloads
items.abstract: Power swings in large Data Centers (DTCs) running Artificial Intelligence (AI) workloads can excite poorly damped modes in power systems. The resulting forced oscillations can lead to flicker, equipment disconnection, or blackouts. This paper investigates the risks of such load fluctuations for different system strengths and damping conditions. Using an analytical approach based on transfer functions, we identify critical DTC locations in the power grid at which load fluctuations could induce the largest forced oscillations and further characterize the harmonic spectrum of the resulting system response. Depending on the frequency and magnitude of the DTC load fluctuations, forced oscillations can become unbounded. The underlying instabilities are classified into saddle-node bifurcations of the forced periodic response and impasse-surface encounters, using Floquet multipliers and the minimum singular value of the algebraic Jacobian. Furthermore, the impact of different duty cycles and harmonic components beyond the fundamental oscillation frequency in square-wave load profiles is analyzed. Finally, the interaction of two oscillating DTCs is investigated for different locations and forcing frequencies, considering both synchronized and unsynchronized operation. The findings can help system operators to define new regulations on the maximum load fluctuations permitted for DTC facilities at specific grid locations, without negatively affecting the stability and operation of the system.

items.title: From Career Ladders to Digital Jungle Gyms: An HRD Theoretical Framework for Understanding Human-AI Interaction in Career Development
items.abstract: Human Resource Development (HRD) professionals face an unprecedented challenge: supporting career development as artificial intelligence becomes an increasingly influential workplace collaborator. Traditional career theories, including Super’s developmental stages, Holland’s person-environment fit, and Hall’s career frameworks, emerged amid relatively predictable advancement and predominantly human interaction, offering limited guidance for AI-mediated workplace learning. This theoretical article proposes the human-AI Career Integration (HACI) framework, synthesizing career development theory, human-computer interaction, and organizational psychology to explain career adaptation through three dynamically interacting dimensions: adaptive collaboration competency, technology-mediated identity formation, and contextual support systems. Drawing on AI’s paradoxical effects, including narrowing performance gaps while the “silicon ceiling” restricts entry-level access, HACI reconceptualizes adaptability as adaptive collaboration competency, extends identity development to technology-mediated contexts, and positions organizational support as central to career resilience. The framework provides a roadmap for research, HRD interventions, and organizational policies fostering meaningful, sustainable, and equitable careers in AI-mediated workplaces.

items.title: From Diagnostic Categories to Design Logic: A Narrative Review of AI-Supportive Systems for Neurodivergent Children
items.abstract: Artificial intelligence and data-driven systems are increasingly embedded in support structures for neurodivergent children; however, approaches often prioritize measurable signals over contextual understanding, creating a disconnect between data-driven representations and the realities of everyday life. This study presents a narrative review of AI-supportive systems using a PRISMA-informed screening process to identify 67 studies published between 2021 and 2026. Findings show that the evidence base is dominated by autism-focused prototype development evaluated under controlled conditions. Support needs are more often involved in validating completed prototypes than in shaping systems during the design process. Research demonstrates technical feasibility more reliably than meaningful benefit in real-world use. In response, this article proposes a Function-Context-Participation framework, arguing that AI-supportive systems should be organized around cross-diagnostic functional needs, evaluated across home, school, and clinical settings, and developed through co-design processes that involve neurodivergent children and their support networks from the earliest stages of design.

items.title: From emergency telework to hybrid workplace learning: a systematic review of digital upskilling, organisational support and performance
items.abstract: Purpose This study aims to systematise research on the transition from emergency telework to structured hybrid work, focusing on employee development, digital upskilling, organisational support and performance. Design/methodology/approach A systematic literature review was conducted using PRISMA. The review analysed 78 studies published between 2020 and 2025, extracted from Web of Science and Scopus, appraised with the Mixed Methods Appraisal Tool and examined through inductive thematic classification. Findings The findings show that hybrid work has evolved from an improvised crisis response into a planned organisational model that requires new forms of employee development and organisational support. Four interrelated clusters were identified: work redesign; human resource management, leadership and culture; health, well-being and work–life balance; and performance, productivity and technology. Sustainable hybrid work depends not only on flexibility but also on autonomy-supportive leadership, perceived organisational support, results-based management and continuous digital upskilling. The review also shows that task-technology fit is central to employee performance and well-being, as digital tools only improve hybrid work outcomes when they are aligned with task requirements, employee capabilities and organisational support systems. Originality/value The study connects hybrid work, workplace learning and employee development, positioning task-technology fit as a strategic HRD issue rather than a purely technical concern.

items.title: From Intents to Algorithms: Verified Algorithm Discovery for Transport Networks
items.abstract: Intent-based networking decouples desired outcomes from device-level configuration, but most systems still map intents to parameters of an algorithm selected in advance. Large language models (LLMs) create an opportunity to automate algorithm design, yet unrestricted generated code is unsuitable for transport-network control because feasibility, reproducibility, and robustness must be enforced independently of the model. We present VERA-TN, a verification-guided framework that compiles a network intent into a bounded algorithm-design specification. The target architecture uses an LLM as a semantic variation operator over typed request-ordering and path-ranking programs; generated logic remains separated from a trusted allocator that enforces path validity, latency, capacity, and single-path constraints. We prove feasibility preservation under explicit assumptions and establish a sufficient bound for the lexicographic latency tie-break in the exact reference model. The released proof-of-concept instantiates the same interface with a bounded ten-parameter numerical candidate and deterministic replay, rather than a completed live-LLM/AST study. Across 150 certified held-out cases on a 28-node TEFNET24-derived hierarchy, evolutionary search reaches a mean priority-utility ratio of 0.958, compared with 0.952 for equal-budget random search and 0.940 for priority-greedy routing. The gain over random search is small but statistically detectable (Holm- adjusted p = 0.0083). The candidate does not improve congestion relative to MILP-C, and the effect of failure-aware training is inconclusive at the 0.05 level (p = 0.051). Eight discovery runs on the official national topology and replay on 12 unseen metro-regional topologies show no stable intent-specific specialization. These results support the trust-boundary and numerical-evolution claims but do not establish a benefit from LLM generation.

items.title: From Literature to ‘ReWA’: Discussing Reproductive Well-being in HCI
items.abstract: Reproductive well-being is shaped by intersecting cultural, religious, gendered, and political contexts, yet current technologies often reflect narrow, Western-centric assumptions. In this literature review, we synthesize findings from 147 peer-reviewed papers published between 2015 and 2025 across HCI, CSCW and social computing, ICTD, digital and public health, and AI for well-being scholarship to map the evolving reproductive well-being landscape. We identify three thematic waves that focused on early access and education, cultural sensitivity and privacy, and AI integration with policy-aware design, and highlight how technologies support or constrain diverse reproductive experiences. Our analysis reveals critical gaps in inclusivity, with persistent exclusions of men and non-binary users, migrants, and users in the Global South. Additionally, we surfaced the significant absence of literature on the role of stakeholders (e.g., husband and family members, household maids and cleaning helping hands, midwife, etc.) in the reproductive well-being space. Drawing on the findings from the literature, we propose the ReWA framework to support reproductive well-being for all agenda through six design orientations associated with: location, culture, and history; polyvocality and agency; rationality, temporality, distributive roles, and methodology.

items.title: From Mediation to Escalation: Buffer Spaces for Workplace Concern Reporting
items.abstract: Workplace concern reporting systems have traditionally been designed around formal channels such as HR portals, grievance procedures, and whistleblower mechanisms. However, employees often perceive these formal systems as opaque, untrustworthy, emotionally draining, and ultimately ineffective, particularly those from marginalized or vulnerable backgrounds. On the other hand, informal channels, such as peer conversations, employee resource groups (ERGs), and backchannel communications, offer alternative spaces for sharing and validating concerns. However, these informal channels also face limitations, including the lack of procedural follow-through and organizational authority, potential social risk, and limited responsiveness. Drawing on 22 interviews with employees and HR professionals, we introduce the concept of buffer spaces —intermediary spaces that overlap informal and formal systems. These spaces help employees emotionally process concerns, assess potential risks, and prepare for escalation, bridging the gap between informal sense-making and formal reporting. We also show the potential of how these spaces mediate the emotional and procedural burdens of existing reporting systems, while also serving as catalysts for organizational change. Our findings call for a reimagining of concern reporting as a dynamic continuum, where concerns develop and evolve through an overlapping space between informal and formal systems rather than as a binary choice between the two.

items.title: From OSS to Open Source AI: an Exploratory Study of Collaborative Development Paradigm Divergence
items.abstract: AI development is embracing open-source paradigm, but the fundamental distinction between AI models and traditional software artifacts may lead to a divergent open-source development paradigm with different collaborative practices, which remains unexplored. We therefore bridge the knowledge gap by quantifying and characterizing the differences in the collaborative development paradigms of traditional open source software (OSS) and open source AI models (OSM), and investigating the underlying factors that may drive these distinctions. We collect 1,428,792 OSS repositories from GitHub and 1,440,527 OSM repositories from HF Hub, and conduct comprehensive statistical, social network and content analyses to measure and understand the differences in collaboration intensity, collaboration openness, and user innovation across the two development paradigms, complementing these quantitative results with semi-structured interviews. In consequence, we find that compared to OSS development paradigm, the OSM development paradigm exhibits significantly lower collaboration intensity; lower collaboration openness regarding direct contribution while persisting relatively open knowledge exchange; and a divergence toward adaptive utilization user-innovation rather than collaborative improvement. Through semi-structured interviews, we further elucidate the socio-technical factors underlying these differences. These findings reveal the paradigmatic divergence in open source development between traditional OSS and OSM across three critical dimensions of open source collaboration and potential underlying factors, shedding light on how to improve collaborative work techniques and practices within the context of AI development.

items.title: From PyTorch to the NPU: LLM-Agent-Driven Model Conversion Across Heterogeneous Inference Runtimes
items.abstract: Edge AI model deployment is a multi-stage engineering process involving model conversion, operator compatibility handling, runtime integration, and precision verification. While prior work has demonstrated agent-based automation for Qualcomm AI Runtime, the broader edge inference runtime ecosystem, including Intel OpenVINO, Rockchip RKNN, NVIDIA TensorRT, and ONNX Runtime, presents distinct toolchains and optimization strategies. This paper extends AIPC (AI Porting Conversion, an LLM agent-driven methodology for AI model deployment automation previously demonstrated on Qualcomm AI Runtime) to multi-runtime scenarios, proposing an LLM agent-driven approach for automated single-model-to-single-runtime deployment across heterogeneous inference backends, such as Intel OpenVINO, Rockchip RKNN, NVIDIA TensorRT, and ONNX Runtime. We decompose the edge AI deployment into standardized, verifiable stages, and inject runtime-specific domain knowledge into the agent execution flow through agent skills, auxiliary scripts, and staged verification loops. Using representative vision models, we demonstrate that agent-based deployment can complete the conversion from a PyTorch model to its executable inference, targeting OpenVINO for x86/NPU, RKNN for RK3588, TensorRT for NVIDIA GPU, and ONNX Runtime for Qualcomm NPU with a focus on FP16 precision deployment feasibility verification. The contributions of this paper primarily lie in providing multi-runtime deployment engineering practice experience, toolchain mapping analysis, a layout-adaptation and inference-replacement layer that removes manual transpose insertion from the agent's repair burden, and an empirical characterization of agent deviation behavior under structured knowledge injection, rather than large-scale systematic benchmarking or cross-runtime operator repair strategy comparison.

items.title: From Usability Barriers to Design Guidelines: Older Adults’ Interaction with Telemedicine Tasks
items.abstract: Older adults often encounter usability barriers in telemedicine, yet these difficulties are not always translated into practical design guidance. This study identified task-level usability barriers and developed and evaluated corresponding design guidelines. In Phase 1, six adults aged 65 years and above completed registration, text consultation, and video consultation tasks using a think-aloud protocol. Five barrier categories were identified and translated into a redesigned prototype. In Phase 2, 30 older adults completed the same tasks using reconstructed original and redesigned interfaces. The redesigned prototype significantly reduced completion time across all three tasks. Task-specific System Usability Scale scores also increased, with significant improvements for registration and video consultation but not text consultation. The findings provide preliminary empirical support for translating observed interaction barriers into age-friendly telemedicine design responses. The study contributes a structured barrier-to-guideline process linking older adults’ task-level difficulties with implementable and empirically evaluated interface design directions.

items.title: Gauge Symmetry Structures and Big Knowledge Assembly Dynamics: Principles of Artificial Science I (1)
items.abstract: Artificial intelligence is rapidly moving from the accumulation and representation of knowledge toward a more difficult problem: the assembly of heterogeneous bodies of knowledge. Knowledge accumulation is not knowledge integration, and knowledge integration is not yet knowledge assembly. Distinct scientific domains differ in objects, semantics, methods, and local representational frames, even when they share deeper mathematical structures. Building on the program of Integration Science, this paper proposes that such cross-disciplinary structures can be transformed in Artificial Science from descriptive correspondences into operational interfaces for knowledge assembly. Gauge symmetry is developed here as the first structural technology of a broader theory of Big Knowledge Assembly Dynamics. The framework begins with a global-to-local structural principle: for cross-domain knowledge assembly, identification of a common structural group precedes the construction of domain-dependent local gauge transformations. A principal knowledge bundle is introduced as the geometric setting in which a global knowledge connection is represented locally by domain-specific gauge potentials. Covariant derivatives distinguish changes of knowledge content from changes of local frame, while curvature measures irreducible local path dependence in assembly. Domain-specific dynamical phases, already developed in prior models of market, reasoning, economic, and AI dynamics, are lifted into a cross-domain geometric setting in which Berry-type phases represent geometric memory. Yang’s non-integrable phase factor supplies the path-dependent parallel-transport operator, and closed-loop transport yields knowledge holonomy. The framework therefore separates local curvature from global holonomy and allows the possibility of global path memory even when local curvature vanishes. To coordinate the geometry of the knowledge base space with transformations in internal knowledge fibers, a Total Knowledge Connection is proposed by combining an affine connection with an internal gauge connection. This structure supports geodesic and variational descriptions of knowledge-assembly paths. A Geodesic-Pareto principle is then formulated cautiously: when a multi-objective assembly problem induces an effective geometric action, stationary efficient paths may be represented by geodesics of the induced geometry. items.title: Gaze-to-Body: Addressing Expressive Gaps of Desktop Users in Hybrid VR Meetings through Gaze-Driven Head-Controlled Avatars
items.abstract: In hybrid VR meetings, where some users join through VR headsets and others connect via desktop interfaces, there is an asymmetry in nonverbal expressiveness: VR users embody avatars that naturally convey attention through head and gaze movements, whereas desktop users are often represented by static avatars due to limited input capabilities and flat screens. This asymmetry can make it harder for VR users to perceive and interpret whom desktop users are attending to and whether attention is reciprocated, potentially hindering mutual understanding and social connection. To address this gap, we present Gaze-to-Body, a system that maps desktop users’ on-screen gaze to their avatar’s head orientation, enhancing the salience of attentional cues. We conducted a user study that systematically varied Head Control Method (Gaze-Driven vs. Head-Oriented) and Display Layout (Gallery view vs. Immersive view) to examine their impact on gaze behavior and social presence. Our results show that gaze-driven avatars significantly increased direct and mutual gaze between desktop and VR participants, particularly in the Gallery view. However, the front-facing setting (i.e., Gallery view), while enhancing the visibility of attentional cues, also diminished desktop users’ sense of social presence. These findings highlight design implications for developing more expressive avatars, more interpretable attentional cues and enhanced social experiences for future hybrid VR meetings.

items.title: Generative AI as a Mediator in Creator Collaboration: Challenges, Design Opportunities, and Concerns
items.abstract: As Generative AI (GenAI) expands beyond individual workflows and becomes increasingly integrated into collaborative creative work, its potential to address the fundamental challenge of building common ground among creators with diverse expertise remains underexplored. Specifically, we lack empirical understanding of how GenAI can mediate collaboration asymmetries among heterogeneous creators. To address this gap, we conducted a multi-method study with narrative writers (N = 10) and visual designers (N = 10) in the context of game development. Our findings demonstrate that GenAI goes beyond individual assistance to serve as a collaborative mediator by aligning creative intent, sustaining shared understanding, and mitigating interpersonal friction among creators. At the same time, we highlight concerns that GenAI may reduce communication among creators, undermine mutual trust, and reshape interpersonal dynamics and collaborative processes. Based on these insights, we identify design opportunities for GenAI tools that nurture collaborative synergy while preserving the creativity and values of human work.

items.title: Generative AI-assisted workflows in architectural conceptual design: Performance, creative self-efficacy, and cognitive load
items.abstract: Generative AI (GenAI) is increasingly adopted in design education, yet evaluating its educational value through final outcomes provides an incomplete picture. This study compares two ecologically plausible workflows in an architectural conceptual design task: GenAI-assisted image generation and ArchDaily-based precedent search. The comparison concerns complete workflows rather than the isolated contributions. Thirty-six students completed a two-phase design task, first designing independently and then revising with their assigned workflow. Screen-recording demonstrated active engagement in both conditions. Eight judges rated design performance, while participants reported task-specific and general creative self-efficacy and cognitive load after each phase. Difference-in-differences analyses showed no significant overall differences between the GenAI and precedent-search workflows in design performance, cognitive workload, or task-specific creative self-efficacy. Beyond these null overall effects, three patterns were observed. General creative self-efficacy showed a significant relative decline under the GenAI workflow. A subgroup analysis suggested higher revision-phase performance among novice students using GenAI than among those using precedent search (F (1,32) = 4.303, p = 0.046, partial η 2 = 0.118). However, this exploratory interaction should be interpreted cautiously due to low rating reliability, small subgroup cells, and imprecise estimation. Third, exploratory prompt analyses suggested that iterative, task-specific prompting strategies (CD3, CD6) were associated with cognitive load reductions at the uncorrected level, but neither association survived multiple-comparison correction. Overall, the GenAI workflow did not produce uniform gains. Its educational value may depend on pedagogical framing, learner characteristics, and human–AI interaction structure, underscoring the need to preserve creative agency and develop prompt literacy.

items.abstract: This experimental prompting study examines how five large language models (LLMs) (ChatGPT, Claude, DeepSeek, Grok, Le Chat) distribute and shape documented disinformation narratives across three conflicts (Russia-Ukraine, Iran-Israel-United States, UK-Russia/Skripal), four user personas, and two languages (English, Norwegian). Responses are coded in two stages, distribution (refusal, narrative absent, narrative present) and shaping (endorsement, normalization, contestation, rejection with or without counter-evidence), analysed using generalized linear mixed models. The study is exploratory and tests no directional hypothesis. This study's also follows GUIDE-LLM, a consensus reporting checklist for LLM use in behavioural science (Feuerriegel et al., 2026)

items.title: Geographical Analysis of Desertification and Environmental Degradation and the Spatial Variation of Their Manifestations in Parts of the Jifara Plain
items.abstract: This research aims to analyze the spatial variation of desertification and environmental degradation manifestations in the Al-Jfara Plain, identify the degrees, intensity, and geographical distribution of desertification, and determine the main manifestations associated with land degradation. It also seeks to identify the effects of natural and human factors on the spread of desertification and determine the areas most vulnerable to it, thereby contributing to efforts to conserve natural resources and reduce land degradation. The research adopted the analytical approach as the main method for analyzing data related to degraded lands, vegetation cover, rangelands, rainfall, erosion, and agricultural and livestock production. It also employed the descriptive approach to present the natural and human characteristics of the research area, as well as the comparative approach to compare different spatial units and time periods. The research further relied on geographical references, scientific studies, and available data, using percentages and rates of change to compare levels of degradation. The research concluded that there is clear spatial variation in the manifestations of desertification and environmental degradation across the Al-Jfara Plain. Wind erosion, declining vegetation cover, drought, and rainfall variability emerged as the most prominent manifestations of degradation. In addition, overgrazing, excessive exploitation of soil and groundwater resources, and urban expansion contributed to increasing pressure on natural resources. The research recommends reducing overgrazing, rationalizing groundwater use, combating erosion, increasing vegetation cover, regulating land use, and enhancing environmental awareness. It also proposes periodic monitoring of desertification using remote sensing and Geographic Information Systems (GIS), preparing updated maps of land degradation, and implementing projects for the rehabilitation of degraded lands.

items.title: Geometry-Conditioned Visual Place Recognition in Natural Environments
items.abstract: Visual Place Recognition (VPR) in natural environments remains challenging due to repetitive vegetation, sparse distinctive landmarks, and substantial appearance and viewpoint variation across traversals. While visual observations of the same place can change considerably, their underlying spatial structure is often more persistent. We exploit this complementary geometric consistency through Depth-Aware Distillation (DAD), which conditions the token representations of a pretrained Vision Foundation Model (VFM) on geometry inferred by a Geometric Foundation Model (GFM), without any depth sensor. Rather than treating geometry as an additional input modality, DAD projects image-aligned depth into the VFM token space and selectively modulates visual representations through channel-wise geometric conditioning. A two-stage teacher-guided learning strategy first anchors the geometry-conditioned representation to the pretrained appearance space, before refining it for place discrimination. Evaluated on the WildCross benchmark, DAD improves average inter-sequence Recall@1 from 61.41% to 66.37% and Recall@5 from 65.86% to 72.49% over a matched appearance-only baseline, with the largest gains under reverse traversal and long-term appearance variation. These results show that GFM-derived geometry can provide a persistent structural prior for VPR when visual appearance becomes unreliable.

items.title: Geospatial embeddings detect old-growth forests but buffered spatial validation narrows their advantage over Sentinel features
items.abstract: Old-growth forests develop over centuries under minimal anthropogenic disturbance, producing structurally complex and biodiverse stands. In Europe, protecting them requires mapping that is accurate for individual forest parcels yet deployable continent-wide. Geospatial foundation model (GFM) embeddings enable label-scarce land classification, but their value for old-growth detection remains unknown. Here, we map old-growth forests across 211,893 ha of Romania's Southern Carpathians, a beech-spruce landscape typical of the Alpine Biogeographic Region. We construct high-confidence, expert-informed reference labels for old-growth and non-old-growth parcels. We add AlphaEarth, TESSERA v2 and Sentinel-1/2 features to a common baseline of topographic and human-access predictors, then compare them under spatially blocked validation with and without 10 km train-test buffers to limit residual autocorrelation. With buffering, GFM and Sentinel-1/2 predictors increase precision-recall AUC by 0.21-0.25 [95% CIs: 0.15-0.34] relative to baseline, indicating spectral data contain a spatially robust old-growth signal. With a PR-AUC of 0.84 [0.79-0.88], TESSERA outperforms Sentinel-1/2 (+0.08 [+0.05 to +0.11]) and AlphaEarth (+0.08 [+0.04 to +0.12]) under unbuffered spatial validation. At a 10 km buffer, however, this advantage narrows to +0.04 [-0.01 to +0.11] and +0.03 [-0.04 to +0.10], intervals consistent with no difference. At 10 m resolution, convolutional neural networks add no benefit over pixel-based XGBoost. Comparisons with four national- and continental-scale products show the importance of non-old-growth labels, and reveal 81% agreement between our predictions and a field-calibrated map. We conclude that buffered spatial validation is vital when transferring old-growth detection models to unseen landscapes, and provide our labels and predictions for future work.

items.title: Giving Care, Seeking Help: Examining the Role of Online Social Platforms for Remote Mental Health Supporters
items.abstract: Remote mental health supporters, family members, partners, and friends assisting their loved ones with mental illness from afar, face heightened risks of psychological distress. To better understand their support needs, we surveyed 154 remote supporters to investigate their online platform use for social support. Remote supporters reported using various platforms (e.g., Reddit, YouTube, and Facebook), with significant differences in perceived quality of the support they receive: Discord rated highest in emotional, informational, and companion support, while YouTube rated the lowest. Our analysis showed that perceived closeness with platform users and likelihood of discussing support were significantly associated with perceived support. Moreover, perceived emotional support and individual loneliness significantly predicted frequency of platform usage. Our findings demonstrate the importance of distinguishing between platforms and their specific supportive functions. Furthermore, features that facilitate closer interactions appear to enhance the perceived social support that remote mental health supporters receive from online communities, potentially improving their caregiving experience. We conclude by discussing design implications for platforms to better support remote mental health caregivers’ emotional, companion, and informational needs.

items.title: GROUND HANDLING PERSONNEL IN UZBEKISTAN'S CIVIL AVIATION: AN OVERLOOKED YET INDISPENSABLE WORKFORCE
items.abstract: Purpose. To analyse the position of ground handling personnel in Uzbekistan's civil aviation sector, a workforce segment that is operationally indispensable yet largely absent from public and academic discussion. Methods. Qualitative analysis of secondary sources (IATA and Boeing industry data, Oxford Economics/ATAG employment analysis, peer-reviewed literature, corporate communications of Uzbekistan Airports and industry reporting for 2021–2026) combined with a comparative analysis of global trends and national conditions. Results. According to IATA, 60% of ground handling professionals report insufficient qualified staff and 37% expect shortages to persist; annual turnover in ground operations averages about 20% and varies widely between operators. In Uzbekistan, a dedicated subsidiary, Uzbekistan Airports Handling LLC, was established in 2021 and training cooperation with Incheon International Airport has begun; however, ground handling still lacks a visible, staged career path comparable to those of pilots and air traffic controllers. Three barriers were identified: organisational framing as a support function, the absence of a progression ladder, and low public visibility. Conclusion. Staffing sustainability requires treating ground handling as a defined profession, with formal qualification tiers, linked pay progression, occupational health protection and public recognition.

According to IATA, 60% of ground handling professionals report insufficient qualified staff and 37% expect shortages to persist; annual turnover in ground operations averages about 20% and varies widely between operators. items.title: GUIAuditor: Enabling Post-hoc Child Safety Forensics via Action-Guided GUI Provenance on Mobile Devices
items.abstract: The proliferation of smart devices exposes children to online risks like grooming and financial scams that are deeply embedded within legitimate applications. Current approaches rely on automated prevention and detection, a paradigm that is fundamentally limited by its inherent fallibility. Whether rule-based or AI-driven, they inevitably produce false positives and negatives, failing to provide reliable protection. In this paper, we argue for a complementary, human-in-the-loop, post-hoc forensic paradigm. We present GUIAuditor, the first system designed to realize this vision by creating GUI Provenance: a queryable, semantic record of a child's interaction sequence. To generate this, GUIAuditor leverages a Multimodal Large Language Model (MLLM) to translate the temporal sequence of GUI events into a human-understandable narrative. To make this practical on mobile devices, a novel evidence distillation pipeline reduces the data requiring analysis by over 89.2% compared to periodic sampling approaches adopted by industry standards, with negligible impact on accuracy. On a new dataset of 295 interaction clips, GUIAuditor achieves a 95.23% Macro-F1 Score in logging significant events and, crucially, its two-stage forensic query engine successfully retrieves the correct evidence as the top result for over 90.20% of natural language questions. An end-to-end evaluation on three modern smartphones shows that the full pipeline, including on-device MLLM inference, adds 2.1W of power draw and 7.4s of per-event latency, with a peak memory footprint of ${\sim}$3.1GB. These results show that post-hoc GUI forensics can run on modern mobile devices and provide useful context for guardian-led safety review.

items.title: Hallucination in Large Language Models: Epistemic Status, Detection, and Validation Criteria in Higher Education
items.abstract: False statements produced by a language model arrive with the same confident form as true ones, with no mark to guide verification, and this indistinction bears fully on the university classroom. This article reviews the peer-reviewed literature under a declared protocol that retained thirty-two works and one continuously updated resource, drawn from technical research on detection, epistemology, cognitive psychology, critical thinking, and educational research. The argument starts from an epistemic and functional characterization of the system, to which we attribute the lack of access of its own to the output and of a criterion of truth of its own, whence it follows that every correction comes from a reference external to the generative process, which we call external anchoring. On that basis, the classes of divergence are ordered according to whether they are measured against facts about the world or against the material supplied by the user, the detection procedures are reviewed together with their declared limits, and four criteria applicable from a public interface are formulated, grouped into two families and crossed with the typology in a table. The closing sections examine two effects on the reader, cognitive satisfaction and the externalization of epistemic vigilance, and the institutional conditions that their correction demands.

items.title: Haptic Guidance Using Electrical Muscle Stimulation for Gesture-based Mobile Robot Teleoperation
items.abstract: In this paper, we propose a virtual reality (VR)-based teleoperation system that utilizes Electrical Muscle Stimulation (EMS) to provide haptic guidance for gesture-based mobile robot control. We develop an operator-independent, posture-aware regression model that predicts wrist movement directions induced by EMS across the control space. This estimation model is integrated into a VR teleoperation system that evaluates obstacle proximity and actuates the user’s muscles to safely steer their gestures away from obstacles, thereby preventing collisions. To validate the efficacy of the proposed system, we conducted a user study comparing EMS guidance, vibration guidance, and no-guidance conditions for a mobile robot teleoperation task. The study revealed that our system provides two distinct benefits. First, as a shared control interface, it significantly improved navigation safety. Second, participants who underwent EMS training maintained improved navigation performance even without guidance. These findings indicate that the proposed method functions effectively as a real-time safety mechanism while supporting the internalization of safer control strategies.

items.title: Has The Physical Layer Matured?
items.abstract: The wireless physical (PHY) layer has enabled successive generations of cellular systems through advances in modulation, coding, waveforms, and multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) transmission. This article assesses whether these techniques are now approaching maturity and where substantial further gains remain possible. Field measurements and quantitative evaluations indicate that many link-level refinements, including constellation shaping, channel-code evolution, reduced-complexity receivers, and waveform enhancements, remain valuable but typically provide bounded gains that must be balanced against implementation complexity and overhead. In contrast, massive MIMO and distributed MIMO offer a more scalable system-level opportunity by increasing the number and quality of usable spatial channels. Their effectiveness relies on time-division duplex reciprocity for scalable channel state information (CSI) acquisition, while practical limitations include calibration, pilot reuse, channel aging, weak pilot reception from cell-edge users, and the fronthaul and synchronization requirements of coherent distributed operation. Artificial intelligence and machine learning (AI/ML) provide complementary opportunities for further PHY layer innovations. The PHY layer is therefore not dead; its most consequential advances will come from deployable spatial processing and CSI acquisition, complemented by targeted link-level and AI/ML-based refinements.

items.title: Health and safety management actions to reduce the impact that medication can have on occupational risks in SMEs
items.abstract: Introduction Occupational risks and accidents are a global concern, so this analysis has been undertaken by a multitude of researchers. However, there is a limited body of research specifically addressing the influence of medication on occupational risks and, more notably, the development of measures aimed at controlling or reducing the impact that such medication may have on workplace safety and health. This scientific gap is even greater among small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs). Methods The general objective of the research presented here is to identify and explore possible health management actions, based on the experience of occupational physicians that could be adopted to reduce the impact of medication on occupational risks in SMEs. To this end, an expert panel was held in May 2023 using the nominal group technique, in which 10 experts in occupational health and safety participated, with open-ended questions, in order to determine these actions. Results The main results were as follows: discourage, reduce, and control self-medication by doctors based on a greater knowledge of the problem by both groups; improve information and training for employers, prevention services, and workers on the side effects and impact of drugs on occupational accidents; unify or integrate the medical-occupational history with the general clinical history of the working population; and establish alarm systems in the IT tools of the healthcare systems. Discussion The study not only contributes to a better understanding of the occupational risks associated with medication, but also provides practical recommendations to mitigate them. The findings identify a set of recommendations that, according to the experts’ assessment, could help improve preventive management related to medication use in the workplace.

items.title: Health conditions and occupational injuries in formal and informal employment: evidence from a national population-based survey in Chile
items.abstract: Abstract Background Informal employment represents a substantial share of the labor force in many middle-income countries and is often associated with weaker occupational safety regulation and limited access to occupational health protections. Although growing evidence suggests that health conditions are associated with occupational injuries, little is known about whether these associations differ between formal and informal employment contexts. This question is particularly relevant in settings where informal employment remains widespread. Methods This study used nationally representative data from the CASEN 2024 survey in Chile. After applying the predefined inclusion criteria and survey expansion weights, the analytical sample represented approximately 8.52 million workers. Survey-weighted logistic regression models accounting for the complex sampling design were used to examine the associations between health conditions, functional limitations, and occupational injuries occurring during the previous three months. Fully adjusted models included demographic, socioeconomic, occupational, and employment-related covariates. Interaction terms were used to assess whether these associations differed between formal and informal workers. Results Overall, 0.75% of workers reported an occupational injury during the three months preceding the survey. Diabetes (AOR = 1.71, 95% CI: 1.16–2.52) and other unspecified health conditions (AOR = 1.88, 95% CI: 1.36–2.59) were significantly associated with higher odds of occupational injury. Among functional limitations, physical or mobility difficulties (AOR = 1.80, 95% CI: 1.26–2.57) and hearing difficulties (AOR = 1.76, 95% CI: 1.09–2.85) were also significantly associated with occupational injury. No statistically significant interactions were observed between health conditions or functional limitations and employment status. Informal workers reported a lower prevalence of occupational injuries, and the sensitivity analysis restricted to injuries requiring medical attention yielded findings generally consistent with the primary analyses. Conclusions Health conditions and functional limitations were associated with higher odds of occupational injuries among Chilean workers. These associations were broadly similar among formal and informal workers, suggesting that health-related vulnerabilities are associated with occupational injury risk across employment contexts. The lower prevalence of reported occupational injuries among informal workers may reflect differences in reporting practices and work interruption behaviors. The main findings remained generally consistent when the analysis was restricted to occupational injuries requiring medical attention. Strengthening occupational health surveillance and prevention strategies that account for workers’ health status across both formal and informal employment contexts may contribute to improving worker safety and reducing occupational injury risk.

items.title: Hierarchical BART for Abstractive Multi-Document Summarisation: A Two-Stage Inference Pipeline with Semantic Evaluation
items.abstract: Synthesising information scattered across multiple related documents into a single readable summary is fundamentally harder than summarising a single text. When documents originate from independent authors, the same event may be described through contrasting lenses, with divergent vocabulary, conflicting details, or complementary facts that no single source captures alone. Neural abstractive models—BART, T5, and PEGASUS—have greatly narrowed the gap to human performance on single-document tasks, yet their fixed 1,024-token encoder window becomes a hard ceiling when applied to multi-document clusters. For news corpora the average cluster runs to roughly 2,200 tokens; for scientific literature it reaches 4,800. Standard truncation therefore quietly throws away 54% and 79% of the source material, respectively—a coverage shortfall that current leaderboards largely obscure. Architectural remedies such as GraphSum, PRIMERA, and TALER partially address this by extending context capacity or re-aligning representations, but each demands substantial engineering overhead—extra GNN layers, specialised pre-training objectives, or delicate adversarial training loops. We introduce HierBART (Hierarchical BART), which sidesteps the need for any of this by treating the limitation as an inference-time problem rather than an architectural one. The approach is deliberately minimal: chunk the token stream into fixed-width overlapping windows, summarise each with a fine-tuned BART-BASE model (Stage 1), concatenate those local summaries into a fusion sequence, and re-decode it through the same model a second time (Stage 2). Because the pipeline uses only a standard fine-tuned checkpoint with unchanged weights, any future improvement to the backbone—quantisation, distillation, better fine-tuning data—automatically carries over. Benchmarked on Multi-News and Multi-XScience, HierBART reaches ROUGE-1 of 45.70 on Multi-News, outstripping TALER by 12.86 points, and 32.68 on Multi-XScience (+4.38). BERTScore F1 (roberta-large) stands at 80.14 and 84.44 respectively. A five-condition validation-set ablation traces 11.73 of the 22.21-point cumulative gain to the two structural decisions—window chunking (+7.17) and two-pass fusion (+4.56)—ruling out decoding artefacts as the driver. Blind human evaluation by five postgraduate NLP students rates HierBART at 7.90/10 for Fluency and 8.10/10 for Informativeness (Fleiss κ = 0.61), confirming that metric gains translate to perceptibly better summaries.

items.title: How Gender Differences and Role Expectations Shape Work-Family Conflict in Remote-Working Parents: A Mixed-Methods Study in Japan
items.abstract: Working parents face significant challenges in balancing work and childcare, which often results in work-family conflict (WFC). Previous work suggests that remote work complicates the management of boundaries between work and home, but WFC among remote working parents remains underexplored. To address this gap, we conducted an online survey (n=1,200) and semi-structured interviews (n=20) with remote workers in Japan with children paying close attention to gender differences. We found that remote-working mothers experience a higher WFC, but a spouse’s understanding of their work role and alignment with the expectations of the management of their work-family role are related to a lower WFC for both genders. In addition, an interaction analysis showed that remote working mothers face higher WFC than fathers, especially when work-centric or eager to conform to workplace norms. Given these findings, we discuss design implications for technologies that support the management of work-family roles for parenting remote workers.

items.title: How Much Were You Told? Measuring External Information in Peer Reviews
items.abstract: Conference policies distinguish using Large Language Models (LLMs) to polish one's own review from delegating the critique, but current Artificial Text Detection (ATD) methods largely measure surface form rather than the origin of its content. We instead measure the external information carried by a review: information not explained by the reviewed paper and a generic reviewing instruction. We propose Self-Conditioning, an unsupervised information-theoretic estimator that compares the likelihood of a review under its production context with its likelihood when that context is augmented with hints extracted from the review itself. On the IntelLabs peer-review benchmark, Self-Conditioning separates fully-delegated from machine-polished reviews with AUC up to $1.0$ while remaining largely insensitive to surface rewriting. Moreover, as generators receive increasing amounts of externally-provided information, their scores move monotonically towards the human regime, unlike standard ATD baselines. High-temperature sampling can evade the estimator, but at the cost of output quality.

items.title: How Spatial Biologists Direct and Verify AI-Assisted Analyses
items.abstract: Spatial biologists use visualization to assess computational analyses of tissue data. We examine how they direct and verify analyses when an AI agent performs this work. We synthesized workflows from fourteen contextual inquiries and conducted a formative pilot followed by an observational study with ten spatial biologists using Claude Science on their own data. Participants valued help with plotting, locating cells of interest, and tasks they found laborious or could not otherwise perform. Assessing the agent's work involved obtaining suitable evidence, sometimes through additional work in external tools, and interpreting it using knowledge of the tissue and its markers. Scientists also sought information about ongoing computation to decide how analysis should proceed. We contribute a workflow synthesis, an empirical account of scientists directing and verifying agentic analyses, and four design directions addressing execution control, familiar interactive views, source and execution information, and accessible verification across computing setups and experience.

items.title: How to Live in a World on Fire: Algorithmic Exploitation, Mutual Aid, and the Struggle for Resilient Futures
items.abstract: As climate disasters intensify, the intersection of computing and crisis response reveals how algorithmic systems routinely exacerbate inequality. Failures such as surge pricing during Hurricane Helene, Starlink’s restricted access in disaster zones, and the collapse of Texas’s power grid during Winter Storm Uri are not aberrations but constitutive features of infrastructures optimized for efficiency and profit. These systems translate vulnerability into market opportunity, reproducing disaster capitalism while neglecting human well-being. In contrast, mutual aid networks rooted in solidarity and community care provided vital support where formal institutions and computational systems fell short. We contribute to CSCW by advancing infrastructures of mutuality—a critical lens that links critique of algorithmic exploitation with design orientations inspired by mutual aid. We argue that infrastructures of mutuality are not ad hoc stopgaps but generative counter-logics that reorient computing toward relationality, transparency, and reciprocity. Extending critical and reflective traditions in CSCW, the notion of infrastructures of mutuality emphasizes the design and maintenance of systems that both meet immediate needs and enact alternative social relations. Drawing on practices of care and commoning, this approach highlights how computing might support solidarity, redundancy, and collective governance, moving beyond descriptive critiques of market-driven crisis informatics toward design futures that sustain just and resilient infrastructures.
